findings.title: Furnished assembly and the audit of social standing
findings.claim: The preceding boast compares the groups by station and gathering, then recalls generations with better furnishings and appearance. 19:75 remeasures that standing through the worse place and weaker supporting host: visible abundance and assembly remain part of the comparison, while the focus exposes how they can be mispriced as security.

The focus's جند can carry a mutually supporting collective and its army/supporter specialization; the earlier council and display trigger that meaning, while the focus's comparative changes the measure from visible display to actual placement and effective backing. The branch-level value/pricing reading is activated by the repeated comparative appraisal, not by a literal exchange.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing comparison reads as an audit of what can sustain a group, not as a denial that its venue, furnishings, or appearance may look superior.
findings.containment: This is a point-by-point contextual reading, while the final comparison could also function as a broader warning. No literal purchase, market, or price is asserted. The HFT branches root_000010/B001 and root_001487/B003 have no supplied lexicon records and remain attributed; their distinct IDs are not merged with root_000010/B002 or root_001486/B001.

findings.title: Extension gives a self-renewing drift room to continue
findings.claim: The sequence in 19:59 can be read as a reproducible drift—loss, following desire, and encounter with deviation—while 19:75 supplies extension for the person in misguidance until the promised event is seen. The interval can therefore host a continuing process, not only lengthen a fixed label.
findings.mechanism: In 19:59 the supplied context order moves from أَضَاعُوا to ٱتَّبَعُوا ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ and then يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا. The focus's extension for the person in misguidance meets that sequence and gives it room to recur; this recurrence is an inference from the ordered acts and the interval, not a statement of a causal loop in the source.
findings.reader_payoff: Misguidance can become legible as behavior renewed within an allowance, while the focus's stated endpoint remains in view.
findings.containment: The contextual roots ت ب ع, ش ه و, غ و ي, and ض ي ع have no independent branch descriptors in this packet and remain attributed to the exact HFT coordinates. The live alternative is that 19:59 lists acts and outcome without asserting feedback; 19:60 also keeps repentance and return visible, so no inevitability or irreversibility is claimed. For root_001407/B002, only the supporting-addition gloss is activated; no separate duration gloss is invented for it.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace supplies exact context anchors and a focus return, but its branch records are unbound and the feedback loop is explicitly an inference with a live alternative.

findings.title: Continuation has different directions and yields
findings.claim: Beside 19:76's increase of those guided, its enduring good deeds, recompense, and return, 19:75's extension within misguidance reads as an adverse counterpart in direction and outcome. The juxtaposition distinguishes prolongation from increase that yields lasting return while preserving both clauses' ordinary readings.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries misguidance into an extended interval; 19:76 then names increase for the guided, what endures, and recompense and return. These independent contextual terms meet the focus's extension and orientation, making direction and eventual yield the comparison rather than extension alone.
findings.reader_payoff: The adjacent verses allow readers to notice that continuation can be measured by where it is directed and what endures or returns.
findings.containment: The paired trajectory is a contextual inference, not a universal causal law. The live alternative is that 19:76 offers a rhetorical contrast without a shared amplification mechanism. The focus's interval is not equated with the positive increase or reward.

epistemic.reason: The exact adjacent Arabic and matching HFT traces support a directional contrast, but the proposed shared trajectory is an inference with an explicit rhetorical alternative; the HFT branch records are legacy_unbound.

findings.title: The same promise vocabulary frames different outcomes
findings.claim: Within the declared pericope, 19:61 says that the Rahman promised gardens to his servants while unseen; 19:75 names the Rahman as the one extending time and says the addressed people will see what they were promised, then specifies punishment or the Hour. The shared epithet and promise language make the extension read as delay before an outcome, not as a competing promise of reward.
findings.mechanism: The promise of gardens and the certainty of that promise in 19:61 meet the focus's passive promise term and its explicit either-or specification. The repeated divine epithet ties the clauses together while their different recipients and outcomes keep them distinct.
findings.reader_payoff: The interval is held beside a favorable promise in the same pericope, so the focus's extension under the Rahman is not mistaken for endorsement of misguidance.
findings.containment: The packet does not make the promised gardens in 19:61 the referent of the focus's promised object; the focus explicitly supplies punishment or the Hour. The relation is a contextual juxtaposition based on exact Arabic, with target morphology for 19:61 unavailable.

epistemic.reason: The exact Arabic in both passages supplies repeated promise wording and the same epithet. The connection row is a nomination, and the relation is kept at phrase level because target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: Human recognition follows an already framed judgment
findings.claim: The focus's future knowing after sight sits within a pericope that has already named those most rebellious against the Rahman, said that God knows best who deserves the fire, and then described the God-fearing as saved while wrongdoers are left there. Its final comparison can therefore be read as delayed human recognition within a judgment the surrounding verses have already framed.
findings.mechanism: The prior clauses in 19:69–70 move from selecting the most defiant to divine knowledge of who deserves burning; 19:75 shifts to the addressed people knowing after they see what was promised; 19:72 supplies a concrete separation of rescue and those left in Hell. The focus's knowing is thus connected to an ordered disclosure and outcome, not made the source of the judgment.
findings.reader_payoff: The comparison of place and host is read as recognition of an outcome, rather than a verdict based only on the opponents' earlier public claims.
findings.containment: The connection nominations do not establish a one-to-one identity among the groups named in 19:69, 19:70, 19:72, and 19:75. Only their supplied Arabic and local sequence are used; target morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The contextual Arabic and ordering are supplied, but the connection targets have no target morphology or lexical analysis. The broader judgment relation remains a bounded contextual inference.

findings.title: A request for aid as an external overlay
findings.claim: As an external overlay, the Fātiḥa's request for aid lets the focus's weaker host be heard alongside a distinct act of seeking help: the focus measures collective backing, while the external line locates aid in an exclusive request to its addressee.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is جُندًا, whose registered core and host/supporter specialization concern a group that can support. The independent trigger at 1:5:4 explicitly asks the addressed one for help. Their contact makes the focus's comparison about effective backing, not only the number or visibility of a group.
findings.reader_payoff: The host's weakness can be distinguished from the separate question of where aid is sought.
findings.containment: This is an analogical overlay, not a claim that 19:75 alludes to 1:5 or that the audiences are identical. Native pericope comparisons remain complete without it; the external phrase adds only the distinct act of asking for aid.

epistemic.reason: Both the focus word and external help-seeking phrase are supplied, and the focus branch has registered core and specialization facets. Their relation is analogical; no source trust label or target morphology is supplied for the external context.
